heading: ## The first turn
goal: Goal: the person plays the game the brief describes on the Stage, made as well as you can make it: every part a player sees is yours to design.
read: Read `BRIEF.md`, `studio-skills/three.md` and the bridge contract in `TEMPLATE.md` (what the harness needs from the game, nothing about how it looks), then build the game in `web/`. Write no plan or design document.
watched: The person watches the Stage while you work: it shows the game from the first frame it draws and follows every save. `web/main.js` is a running stand-in: replace its scene with the game's first, then grow the game in place.

made.any: made where each comes out best: Blender for characters, creatures and anything sculpted or hard-surface (studio-skills/art-pipeline.md), three.js code for what is quicker there, one at a time once the game plays, each replacing a quick stand-in when it looks better
made.blender: made in Blender (studio-skills/art-pipeline.md), after the whole game plays with quick models in code standing in, one at a time, each replacing its stand-in once it looks better
made.code: built in three.js code, never bare primitives standing in for them

library: The person turned the asset library on: use its models where it has what the brief names (`game_assets` op `search`; the first `add` takes `lock`), and the rest are {made}.
chosen: The person chose how the game's models are made: its player, main threat and world are {made}.
anyRoute: You choose how each model is made. Blender is here and recommended for the player, characters, creatures and anything sculpted or hard-surface (studio-skills/art-pipeline.md); three.js code is fine for what is quicker there. Build the whole game first with quick models in code standing in, so the person plays it, then make the real models one at a time, each replacing its stand-in once it looks better. If `game_blender` finds no Blender, build them in code and tell the person that Settings → Game tools takes a Blender.
reference: The person attached a picture to aim for, attached here and saved as `art/reference.png`. When it holds more than the one view you will match (a phone screenshot, a page around it), save that view alone over it. The model sheet and the check show it beside yours.
